clue.text: Change Labour party: use consultants for new style

indicators.note: to change something is to alter it, so the following letters must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A political slogan urging Labour to rebrand by hiring image consultants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' reads as a political demand, but it only tells you to rearrange LABOUR PARTY USE into BEAUTY PARLOURS.
explanation.definitionFit: Salons where hairdressers and beauticians advise clients on a fresh look can be playfully described as places you consult about a makeover.

clue.text: Jump on this bus, not a cycle, after crash

indicators.note: after a crash things lie wrecked and jumbled, so the letters come out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to a commuter whose bicycle was wrecked: hop on the bus instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jump on this bus' looks like one instruction, but the definition stops at 'this'; the fodder is BUS NOT A CYCLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflatable play structure at children's parties is made for leaping about on, so it is something you jump on.

clue.text: One put on scales going over this

definitions.text: One put on scales going over this

parts.note: surface reading: a weight someone places on a weighing balance

parts.words: One put on scales going over this
parts.note: setter's reading: a creature whose body is covered in overlapping scales, which go over it

explanation.surface: Someone loading weights onto a weighing machine and checking the reading.
explanation.walkthrough: The scales are the reptile's skin, not a weighing machine; and 'One put on scales' also hints at someone adding weight.
explanation.definitionFit: The common European viper is a snake, and snakes have scales covering their whole body.

clue.text: Did value fine stamp for collection

indicators.note: a collection gathers things in, so one piece is taken inside another

parts.note: to stamp is to tread heavily
'Fine!' and 'Sure!' both express agreement

explanation.surface: Someone who prized a valuable stamp in their philatelic collection.
explanation.walkthrough: The stamp sounds postal but is the verb tread; 'fine' as a word of assent gives SURE, which goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: If you treasured something you held it dear and cherished it, a past-tense verb matching 'did value'.

clue.text: Delighted prince getting let out

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for prince
property let out is leased

explanation.surface: A prince thrilled to be released from confinement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let out' suggests freedom, but here it means rented to a tenant.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone feeling happy and satisfied, so they are close synonyms as adjectives.

clue.text: Sits around first and rests

indicators.note: what comes first is placed at the front, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a model sits or poses for a portrait

explanation.surface: Someone lolling about before settling down for a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sits' means models for an artist; 'around' as 'about' gives RE, which goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To repose is to lie at ease or take a rest, so the third-person verb matches.

clue.text: Perfume from men about to cheat on you

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it on all sides

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece sitting on another comes above it

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle them
U is text-speak for you

explanation.surface: A tell-tale scent revealing a partner's infidelity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheat on you' reads as betrayal, but 'on' is positional: in a down entry, one piece placed on another sits above it.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfume is a smell, and odour is a general word for any scent, pleasant or otherwise.

clue.text: Reason to restrict booze

parts.note: to ration is to restrict the amount allowed
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A justification for limiting drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reason to restrict booze' reads as one phrase; 'to' is merely the join between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the underlying justification or logic behind a decision, a noun synonym for reason.

clue.text: Security organisation cut short fight that's excessive

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: the United Nations, which has a Security Council
a duel is a formal fight between two

explanation.surface: A security body halting a brawl that has gone too far.
explanation.walkthrough: The Security Council belongs to the UN; DUEL loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Undue means unwarranted or more than is appropriate, an adjective meaning the same as excessive.

clue.text: Uses old charts to get around India

parts.note: ex- means former

indicators.note: getting around something means encircling it, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: to plot is to chart a course or graph
I is India in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A traveller navigating India with outdated maps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charts' look like maps but act as the verb plots; I goes inside it, after EX.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit something is to make use of it, often selfishly, so exploits is a verb synonym of uses.

clue.text: Row following meeting in part of factory

indicators.note: following means coming after, so this piece is placed second

parts.note: an assembly is a gathering or meeting
a row is a line

explanation.surface: An argument breaking out after a workplace meeting on the factory floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' tempts as a quarrel, but it means a line, placed after the meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A production line in a plant, where workers or machines add components in sequence, is a section of a factory.

clue.text: My son has sixth sense around group of mummies?

parts.note: 'Cor!' is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'My!'

indicators.note: turning around faces the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: extrasensory perception
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent boasting that their child can sense the presence of mothers or ghosts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mummies' suggests mothers, but means embalmed bodies; the question mark flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: Mummies are preserved dead bodies, so a bunch of them are dead bodies: the answer defined by example.

clue.text: Drug to port smuggled by suspect that's dangerous

indicators.note: smuggled goods are carried concealed inside something, so one piece hides within another

parts.note: sus is slang for suspicious or a suspect
E is ecstasy
Rio de Janeiro is a port city

explanation.surface: A suspect running drugs into a harbour, which is a risky business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' is not a link here: it joins the drug and the port into one piece before the suspect swallows it.
explanation.definitionFit: A serious injury or illness is a grave one, so the adjective can mean dangerous.

clue.text: One quotes King, penning short article

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, as livestock in a pen, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: Carolus Rex, King Charles

indicators.note: something short is missing its tail, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: an item is an article, as in a newspaper

explanation.surface: A writer quoting Stephen King in a brief piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King' looks like the author but is CR, Charles the king; the article is a newspaper ITEM, not 'a' or 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A citer is someone who cites, and to cite a source is to quote or refer to it.

clue.text: Take out women paid for by party; one might kick back in this

definitions.text: one might kick back in this

indicators.note: out can mean out of order or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
W is the abbreviation for women
a round that is 'on me' is paid for by me
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Taking women on a date funded by a party, where people relax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kick back' sounds like relaxing, but in this martial art you literally kick back at an opponent. 'By' simply places the pieces in sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Taekwondo is a Korean martial art famous for high and spinning kicks, so a fighter might kick back during a bout.

clue.text: Daughter eats ice cream, initially is prepared to dry up

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter

indicators.note: to prepare something is to get it into shape, so the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: first letter of cream

explanation.surface: A daughter eating ice cream, though it is not ready yet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' applies only to the last word before it, so 'eats' and 'ice' go into the mix whole.
explanation.definitionFit: To desiccate is to remove all moisture, as with desiccated coconut, so it means to dry out.

clue.text: Callas in production keeping so elegant

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside
a production reworks material into something new, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
sic is Latin for 'so' or 'thus'

explanation.surface: The soprano Maria Callas staying graceful on stage in an opera production.
explanation.walkthrough: Maria Callas was a famous opera singer, but her name is only letters to rearrange around SIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Classical style is restrained, refined and graceful in the manner of ancient Greece and Rome, so it can mean elegant.

clue.text: Drug to have sex? It might slow you down

parts.note: speed is slang for amphetamine
hump is vulgar British slang for having sex

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether a pill will boost their sex life, then warned it could sedate them.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sounds like a warning about drug side effects. A speed hump is a raised strip across a road; Americans call it a speed bump.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised ridge across a road forces drivers to brake, which is exactly what it is designed for.

clue.text: Dwarf raised leg

parts.note: something raised is up
a leg of a journey is a stage

explanation.surface: A small person lifting a leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dwarf' looks like a noun, but it is the verb meaning to make someone seem small.
explanation.definitionFit: To upstage someone is to outshine them and draw attention away, just as to dwarf is to overshadow.

clue.text: Saw deliveries bowled with spin

parts.note: PR, public relations, is the business of spin
in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries from one bowler
B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: Watching a cricketer bowl spin.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture hides PR as spin; 'saw' is not seeing but a noun for an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim, so it is a synonym of a traditional proverb.

clue.text: One case of beer switched for bitter

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards

indicators.note: switching two things swaps their places, so the pair runs the other way
a case is the outside of something, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: outer letters of beer

explanation.surface: Swapping a crate of lager for a pint of bitter, the British pale ale.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British style of beer, so the surface stays in the pub, but here it is the definition, an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerb is a rare form of acerbic, meaning sharp or sour in taste or manner, so it equals bitter.

clue.text: Briefs of wife found in sheets

indicators.note: what is found in something lies inside it

parts.note: sheets of material are layers
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A wife's underpants turning up in the bed linen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefs' looks like underwear, but in British slang a brief is a lawyer, especially a defence barrister.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a brief is a solicitor or barrister who handles your case, so briefs are legal counsel.

clue.text: Each container to corrode

parts.note: ea. is the abbreviation for each
a tin is a container

explanation.surface: Each can rusting away.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures rust on tins; the phrasal verb is the answer, not dining at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid or rust that eats in gradually wears into a surface, which is what corrosion does.

clue.text: Piece together back of diplodocus, say — our bones kept here

indicators.note: piecing together assembles bits into a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered
the back of something is its end, so only the last letter is kept

parts.note: last letter of diplodocus
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Museum staff reassembling a dinosaur skeleton stored on their premises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example', but it is fodder along with OUR and the S.
explanation.definitionFit: An ossuary is a vault, chamber or container where the bones of the dead are stored.

clue.text: Like fence and tree

parts.note: as means like
to fence in animals is to pen them

explanation.surface: Something resembling both a fence and a tree, perhaps a hedge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fence' looks like a noun but works as the verb meaning to enclose.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspen is a poplar with trembling leaves, one kind of tree, so this is definition by example.

clue.text: Found fake Titian that is for framing

indicators.note: a frame goes around a picture, so these letters go around the others

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

indicators.note: a fake is made up, so the letters are rearranged into something new

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Discovering a forged Titian painting ready to be framed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past tense of find, but it is the verb to establish. Titian was a Venetian Renaissance painter.
explanation.definitionFit: To initiate is to start or set something up, as to found an institution is to establish it.

clue.text: Cold month mostly for island

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a month of the year

explanation.surface: Escaping a chilly month by going to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The cold month seems to be December or January, but it is APRIL with its tail removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an Italian isle in the Bay of Naples, an example of an island.

clue.text: Equalise in match, getting behind marker

indicators.note: something getting behind comes after, so this piece is placed second

parts.note: a counter is a token or marker in a board game
to match is to balance, as accounts do

explanation.surface: A footballer scoring an equaliser after trailing a marking defender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' and 'marker' suggest football, but match is the verb and the marker is a game piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To counterbalance is to offset a weight or force with an equal one, so it means to even things up.
